subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: A cross section is the flat two-dimensional figure you get when a plane slices through a solid. For each problem, decide which two of the solid's dimensions are exposed by the slice, name the resulting shape precisely, and compute its perimeter or area when asked. Give exact values.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ in long, $5$ in wide, and $2$ in tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down through the prism, perpendicular to the length, slicing across the $5$ in by $2$ in face. Name the cross section and give its dimensions.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the length exposes the face whose dimensions are the width and the height.
The width is $5$ in and the height is $2$ in.
Since these two lengths are not equal, the cross section is a rectangle, not a square.
The cross section is a $5$ in by $2$ in rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $10$ cm long, $7$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall. A vertical plane slices straight down, perpendicular to the width, cutting the $10$ cm by $3$ cm face. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.answer: A $10$ cm by $3$ cm rectangle with area $30 \text{ cm}^2$.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the width exposes the length and the height.
The exposed dimensions are $10$ cm and $3$ cm, so the cross section is a rectangle.
Area of a rectangle is length times width: $10 \times 3 = 30$.
The cross section is a $10$ cm by $3$ cm rectangle with area $30 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $6$ cm by $6$ cm by $9$ cm, where the $6$ cm by $6$ cm faces are the top and bottom. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the bottom, slicing through opposite vertical edges. Name the cross section and find its perimeter.
items.answer: A $6$ cm by $9$ cm rectangle with perimeter $30$ cm.

steps: The top and bottom are $6$ cm by $6$ cm, so the prism is $6$ cm by $6$ cm at the base and $9$ cm tall.
A vertical slice exposes one horizontal dimension ($6$ cm) and the height ($9$ cm).
The cross section is a rectangle measuring $6$ cm by $9$ cm.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a rectangular base $12$ ft by $8$ ft. A vertical plane passes through the apex and is parallel to the $12$ ft base edges, slicing the pyramid into two congruent halves. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A plane through the apex of a pyramid cuts down to the base, meeting it in a single line segment.
The cross section has the apex as one vertex and a segment of the base as the opposite side.
A figure with a single top vertex and a base segment is a triangle.
The cross section is a triangle (not the smaller rectangle you would get from a base-parallel slice).

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10$ m by $10$ m and a height of $12$ m. A vertical plane passes through the apex and is parallel to a pair of base edges, cutting the pyramid exactly in half. The base of the resulting triangular cross section spans the full $10$ m base width, and its height equals the pyramid's height. Find the area of this triangular cross section.

steps: A slice through the apex of the pyramid produces a triangle.
Its base is the full base width: $10$ m. Its height is the pyramid's height: $12$ m.
Area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 12 = \frac{1}{2} \times 120 = 60$.
The cross section has area $60 \text{ m}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $7$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices the prism parallel to a $4$ cm by $4$ cm face. Name the cross section precisely and find its area.
items.answer: A $4$ cm by $4$ cm square with area $16 \text{ cm}^2$.

steps: A slice parallel to a face produces a cross section congruent to that face.
The $4$ cm by $4$ cm face has two equal sides, so the cross section is a square.
Area $= 4 \times 4 = 16$.
The cross section is a $4$ cm by $4$ cm square with area $16 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $9$ in by $6$ in by $5$ in. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the $9$ in length, exposing the $6$ in by $5$ in face. Name the cross section and find its perimeter.
items.answer: A $6$ in by $5$ in rectangle with perimeter $22$ in.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the length exposes the width ($6$ in) and the height ($5$ in).
Because $6 \neq 5$, the cross section is a rectangle, not a square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $\frac{5}{2}$ ft long, $4$ ft wide, and $3$ ft tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the width, exposing the length and the height. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.answer: A $\frac{5}{2}$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle with area $\frac{15}{2} \text{ ft}^2$.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the width exposes the length ($\frac{5}{2}$ ft) and the height ($3$ ft).
The cross section is a rectangle with these two dimensions.
Area $= \frac{5}{2} \times 3 = \frac{15}{2}$.
The cross section is a $\frac{5}{2}$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle with area $\frac{15}{2} \text{ ft}^2$ (that is $7.5 \text{ ft}^2$).

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $14$ cm by $6$ cm and a height of $9$ cm. A vertical plane passes through the apex parallel to the $6$ cm base edges, so the triangular cross section has a base of $14$ cm (the full length) and a height equal to the pyramid's height. Find the area of the cross section.

steps: Slicing through the apex gives a triangular cross section.
The triangle's base is the full length $14$ cm and its height is the pyramid height $9$ cm.
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 14 \times 9 = \frac{1}{2} \times 126 = 63$.
The cross section has area $63 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ cm by $8$ cm by $11$ cm, with the $8$ cm by $8$ cm faces on top and bottom. A vertical plane slices straight down, perpendicular to the base, through the centers of two opposite top edges. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.answer: An $8$ cm by $11$ cm rectangle with area $88 \text{ cm}^2$.

steps: The prism is $8$ cm by $8$ cm at the base and $11$ cm tall.
A vertical slice exposes one horizontal dimension ($8$ cm) and the height ($11$ cm).
Since $8 \neq 11$, the cross section is a rectangle, not a square.
Area $= 8 \times 11 = 88 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $12$ mm by $3$ mm by $3$ mm. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the $12$ mm length, exposing a $3$ mm by $3$ mm face. Name the cross section precisely and find its perimeter.
items.answer: A $3$ mm by $3$ mm square with perimeter $12$ mm.

steps: A cut perpendicular to the length exposes the width and height, both $3$ mm.
Two equal sides means the cross section is a square.
Perimeter $= 4 \times 3 = 12$ mm.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a square base $8$ in by $8$ in and a height of $10$ in. A vertical plane passes through the apex parallel to a pair of base edges. The triangular cross section has a base equal to the full $8$ in base edge and a height equal to the pyramid's height. Find the area of the cross section.

steps: A plane through the apex produces a triangle.
Its base is $8$ in (the full base edge) and its height is $10$ in (the pyramid's height).
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 10 = \frac{1}{2} \times 80 = 40$.
The cross section has area $40 \text{ in}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $15$ cm by $9$ cm by $4$ cm. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the $9$ cm width, exposing the length and the height. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.answer: A $15$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle with area $60 \text{ cm}^2$.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the width exposes the length ($15$ cm) and the height ($4$ cm).
The cross section is a rectangle with these dimensions.
Area $= 15 \times 4 = 60$.
The cross section is a $15$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle with area $60 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $6$ in, with the $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $\frac{7}{2}$ in faces on top and bottom. A plane slices the prism parallel to the top face. Name the cross section precisely and find its area.
items.answer: A $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $\frac{7}{2}$ in square with area $\frac{49}{4} \text{ in}^2$.

steps: A slice parallel to the top face is congruent to that face.
The top face is $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $\frac{7}{2}$ in, with two equal sides, so the cross section is a square.
Area $= \frac{7}{2} \times \frac{7}{2} = \frac{49}{4}$.
The cross section is a $\frac{7}{2}$ in by $\frac{7}{2}$ in square with area $\frac{49}{4} \text{ in}^2$ (that is $12.25 \text{ in}^2$).

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $20$ ft by $6$ ft and a height of $7$ ft. A vertical plane passes through the apex parallel to the $6$ ft base edges, producing a triangular cross section whose base is the full $20$ ft length and whose height equals the pyramid's height. Name the cross section and find its area.

steps: A plane through the apex of the pyramid produces a triangular cross section.
The triangle's base is the full length $20$ ft and its height is the pyramid height $7$ ft.
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 7 = \frac{1}{2} \times 140 = 70$.
The cross section is a triangle with area $70 \text{ ft}^2$.
